senses.gloss: f. ch. (preced.) = h. חֶרְיָה, a dried-up twig, hardened palm-twig, opp. כפות flexible.
units: <cite ref="Bava Batra 161b:3">B. Bath. 161ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Gittin 36a:9">Gitt. 36</cite>, a. e. <he>צייר ח׳</he> drew a palm-twig (as his signature). [<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 60:21">Targ. Is. LX, 21</cite> <he>דחרותי</he> ed. Ven., read: <he>דחדותי</he>, v. <cite ref="H00179"><he>חֶדְוָא</he></cite>.]—Pl. <cite ref="H01620"><he>חֶרְוָתָא</he></cite>, <he>חֶרְוָו׳</he>.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 101b:5">B. Bath. 101ᵇ</cite> <he>דעביד להו כי ח׳</he> he makes the burial caves like palm-twigs (in the shape of a fan).

<cite ref="Pesachim 82a">Pes. 82ᵃ</cite> <he>קני ותרוותא</he> Ms. M. 2 (Ms. M. 1 <he>קני דחרות׳</he>, corr. <he>וח׳</he>, ed. <he>וחריואתא</he>, read: <he>וחֶרְוָואתָא</he>; Ar. <cite ref="H01706"><he>חֶרְיָתָא</he></cite>, fr. <cite ref="H01671"><he>חֶרְיָא</he></cite>) reeds and twigs.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 2:3:5">Y. Shebi. II, 33ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>בכנישתא חדתא וחֶרְוָותָה</he> (read: <he>דח׳</he>) with a new broom of palm-twigs.
